__FB_ANDROID__.title: __FB_ANDROID__
__FB_ANDROID__.description: Define without a value created at compile time when the Android target is being used. It can be used to compile parts of a program only for Android.

__FB_ARCH__.name: __FB_ARCH__
__FB_ARCH__.title: __FB_ARCH__
__FB_ARCH__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro string) set by the compiler
__FB_ARCH__.description: Defined as a string literal containing the effective target architecture selected by the compiler, after applying options such as -arch. The value is the compiler's canonical architecture name, not the original option text.

__FB_ARG_COUNT__.name: __FB_ARG_COUNT__
__FB_ARG_COUNT__.title: __FB_ARG_COUNT__
__FB_ARG_COUNT__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro) performed by the compiler.
__FB_ARG_COUNT__.description:
Counts the number of arguments in the argument list (args...) and returns the corresponding value. A value is always returned, with 0 corresponding to an empty argument list.

Because the argument separator is the comma (,), the returned value for a non-empty argument list is the number of main commas (non-nested) plus 1.

__FB_ARG_EXTRACT__.name: __FB_ARG_EXTRACT__
__FB_ARG_EXTRACT__.title: __FB_ARG_EXTRACT__
__FB_ARG_EXTRACT__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro) performed by the compiler.
__FB_ARG_EXTRACT__.description:
Returns the argument from the argument list (args...) corresponding to the index value (index).

If the requested index value refers to an argument that does not exist in the supplied argument list (index value too large), nothing is returned.

__FB_ARG_LEFTOF__.name: __FB_ARG_LEFTOF__
__FB_ARG_LEFTOF__.title: __FB_ARG_LEFTOF__
__FB_ARG_LEFTOF__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro) performed by the compiler.
__FB_ARG_LEFTOF__.description:
Returns the left token of the argument (arg), based on the separator (sep). (in the expression of the argument, the tokens and the separator must be spaced)

By default, if the default return (ret) is not given, the macro returns nothing (empty token) if the separator (sep) is not found. Otherwise, if the default return (ret) is given, the macro returns the default return (ret) if the separator (sep) is not found.

__FB_ARG_LISTEXPAND__.name: __FB_ARG_LISTEXPAND__
__FB_ARG_LISTEXPAND__.title: __FB_ARG_LISTEXPAND__
__FB_ARG_LISTEXPAND__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro) performed by the compiler.
__FB_ARG_LISTEXPAND__.description:
Expands to one or more 'macroname( .... )' depending on the value of macroargcount and number of arguments in the args... list.

Returns empty string on invalid index, rather than compile error.

__FB_ARG_RIGHTOF__.name: __FB_ARG_RIGHTOF__
__FB_ARG_RIGHTOF__.title: __FB_ARG_RIGHTOF__
__FB_ARG_RIGHTOF__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro) performed by the compiler.
__FB_ARG_RIGHTOF__.description:
Returns the right token of the argument (arg), based on the separator (sep). (in the expression of the argument, the tokens and the separator must be spaced)

By default, if the default return (ret) is not given, the macro returns nothing (empty token) if the separator (sep) is not found. Otherwise, if the default return (ret) is given, the macro returns the default return (ret) if the separator (sep) is not found.

__FB_BUILD_FORK_ID__.name: __FB_BUILD_FORK_ID__
__FB_BUILD_FORK_ID__.title: __FB_BUILD_FORK_ID__
__FB_BUILD_FORK_ID__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro string) set by the compiler
__FB_BUILD_FORK_ID__.description:
Substituted by a string of the compiler's custom defined project fork identifier name if defined at fbc build time, or an empty string if it was not defined.

This value is an empty string for releases made by the FreeBASIC Development Team. Community developers and experimenters may define this value when building their own fbc packages using the makefile to help users identify that fbc may be a special build and may have specific features not in the main release packages.

__FB_BUILD_SHA1__.name: __FB_BUILD_SHA1__
__FB_BUILD_SHA1__.title: __FB_BUILD_SHA1__
__FB_BUILD_SHA1__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro string) set by the compiler
__FB_BUILD_SHA1__.description: Substituted by a string of the compiler's source SHA-1 revision. The value is set using the SHA-1 commit id of the source code revision used to build the compiler binary, if available. If the SHA-1 was not available at the time of building the compiler, the value will be an empty string.

__FB_CYGWIN__.name: __FB_CYGWIN__
__FB_CYGWIN__.title: __FB_CYGWIN__
__FB_CYGWIN__.summary: Intrinsic define set by the compiler
__FB_CYGWIN__.description: Define without a value created at compile time in the Cygwin version of the compiler, or when the -target cygwin command line option is used. It can be used to compile parts of the program only if the target is Cygwin.

__FB_DARWIN__.name: __FB_DARWIN__
__FB_DARWIN__.title: __FB_DARWIN__
__FB_DARWIN__.summary: Intrinsic define set by the compiler
__FB_DARWIN__.description: Define without a value created at compile time in the Darwin version of the compiler, or when the -target darwin command line option is used. It can be used to compile parts of the program only if the target is Darwin.

__FB_DEBUG__.name: __FB_DEBUG__
__FB_DEBUG__.title: __FB_DEBUG__
__FB_DEBUG__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro value) set by the compiler
__FB_DEBUG__.description:
__FB_DEBUG__ indicates if the the generate debug information option -g or the enable intrinsic define __FB_DEBUG__ option Compiler Option: -edebug was specified on the command line at the time of compilation.

Returns non-zero (-1) if either option was specified. Returns zero (0) otherwise.

__FB_ERR__ can be used to determine in user source code if the -g or -edebug option was specified or implied on the command line.

__FB_DOS__.name: __FB_DOS__
__FB_DOS__.title: __FB_DOS__
__FB_DOS__.summary: Intrinsic define set by the compiler
__FB_DOS__.description: Define without a value created at compile time if compiling for the DOS target. Default in the DOS hosted version, or active when the -target dos command line option is used. It can be used to compile parts of the program only if the target is DOS. Note: the DOS hosted version cannot compile to other targets than DOS by now.

__FB_DRAGONFLY__.name: __FB_DRAGONFLY__
__FB_DRAGONFLY__.title: __FB_DRAGONFLY__
__FB_DRAGONFLY__.description: Define without a value created at compile time when the DragonFly BSD target is being used. It can be used to compile parts of a program only for DragonFly BSD.

__FB_ENTRY__.name: __FB_ENTRY__
__FB_ENTRY__.title: __FB_ENTRY__
__FB_ENTRY__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro string) set by the compiler
__FB_ENTRY__.description: Defined as a string literal containing the custom entry point specified with -entry. It is an empty string when no custom entry point was specified.

__FB_ERR__.name: __FB_ERR__
__FB_ERR__.title: __FB_ERR__
__FB_ERR__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro value) set by the compiler
__FB_ERR__.description:
__FB_ERR__ indicates if -e, -ex, or -exx was specified on the compiler command line at the time of compilation of a module.

__FB_ERR__ indicates if -earray, -enullptr, or -elocation was specified on the compiler command line, or implied by use of -exx, at the time of compilation of a module.

__FB_ERR__ indicates if -edebug, -edebuginfo, or -eassert was specified on the compiler command line, or implied by use of -g, at the time of compilation of a module.

__FB_ERR__ indicates if -eunwind was specified on the compiler command line, or implied by use of -e, -ex, or -exx, at the time of compilation of a module.

__FB_ERR__ indicates if -earraydims was specified on the compiler command line, or implied by use of -exx, at the time of compilation of a module.

Returns bit-wise OR of the following values:

__FB_ERR__ is always defined.

__FB_EVAL__.name: __FB_EVAL__
__FB_EVAL__.title: __FB_EVAL__
__FB_EVAL__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro) performed by the compiler.
__FB_EVAL__.description:
Evaluates the argument (constant-expression) at compile time.

When the argument evaluation produces a string, __FB_EVAL__ returns a string formatted with a preprocessor operator: - a Non-Escaped String Literal (of form: $"text"), - or an Escaped String Literal (of form: !"text") if needed. For other datatypes produced, simple Literals (of Integers, Floating Points, Booleans) without prefix/suffix are returned.

__FB_EVAL__ macro is useful where there is any of the following: - non functional expression (i.e. side-effects), - needs to be evaluated (i.e. simplified, respecting the operator precedence) before passing it on, - used in a place where fbc would not allow an expression.

__FB_EXPORT__.name: __FB_EXPORT__
__FB_EXPORT__.title: __FB_EXPORT__
__FB_EXPORT__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro value) set by the compiler
__FB_EXPORT__.description: Returns non-zero (-1) when exporting symbols has been enabled with -export, or zero (0) otherwise.

__FB_FPMODE__.name: __FB_FPMODE__
__FB_FPMODE__.title: __FB_FPMODE__
__FB_FPMODE__.summary: Intrinsic define set by the compiler
__FB_FPMODE__.description: Defined as "fast" if SSE fast arithmetics is enabled, or "precise" otherwise.

__FB_FPU__.name: __FB_FPU__
__FB_FPU__.title: __FB_FPU__
__FB_FPU__.summary: Intrinsic define set by the compiler
__FB_FPU__.description:
For x86 and x86_64 targets: - Defined as "sse" if SSE floating point arithmetics is enabled, and - defined as "x87" otherwise

For arm and aarch64 targets: - Defined as "neon" if Advanced SIMD (Neon) extension is enabled, and - defined as "x87" otherwise

__FB_FREEBSD__.name: __FB_FREEBSD__
__FB_FREEBSD__.title: __FB_FREEBSD__
__FB_FREEBSD__.summary: Intrinsic define set by the compiler
__FB_FREEBSD__.description: Define without a value created at compile time in the FreeBSD version of the compiler, or when the -target freebsd command line option is used. It can be used to compile parts of the program only if the target is FreeBSD.

__FB_GCC__.name: __FB_GCC__
__FB_GCC__.title: __FB_GCC__
__FB_GCC__.summary: Intrinsic define set by the compiler
__FB_GCC__.description: Defined to true (-1) if -gen gcc is used, or false (0) otherwise.

__FB_GFXLIB3__.name: __FB_GFXLIB3__
__FB_GFXLIB3__.title: __FB_GFXLIB3__
__FB_GFXLIB3__.summary: Intrinsic define set when gfxlib3 is selected.
__FB_GFXLIB3__.description:
The compiler defines __FB_GFXLIB3__ when the -gfx3 option selects the opt-in gfxlib3 runtime. A source file can make the same selection by defining the symbol before it first includes fbgfx.bi. Including fbgfx3.bi also defines it before loading the common graphics declarations.

The symbol is defined without a value. Test it with ifdef or defined() instead of treating it as a numeric expression.

__FB_GOSUB_SETJMP__.name: __FB_GOSUB_SETJMP__
__FB_GOSUB_SETJMP__.title: __FB_GOSUB_SETJMP__
__FB_GOSUB_SETJMP__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro value) set by the compiler
__FB_GOSUB_SETJMP__.description: Returns non-zero (-1) when the setjmp/longjmp implementation of GOSUB is enabled with -z gosub-setjmp, or zero (0) otherwise.

__FB_GUI__.name: __FB_GUI__
__FB_GUI__.title: __FB_GUI__
__FB_GUI__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro value) set by the compiler
__FB_GUI__.description:
__FB_GUI__ indicates whether GUI subsystem mode is active at the current point in compilation.

Returns non-zero (-1) if the executable subsystem option -s gui was specified, or if #pragma gui is active. Returns zero (0) otherwise.

__FB_HAIKU__.name: __FB_HAIKU__
__FB_HAIKU__.title: __FB_HAIKU__
__FB_HAIKU__.description: Define without a value created at compile time when the Haiku target is being used. It can be used to compile parts of a program only for Haiku.

__FB_IIF__.name: __FB_IIF__
__FB_IIF__.title: __FB_IIF__
__FB_IIF__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro) performed by the compiler.
__FB_IIF__.description:
__FB_IIF__ returns source code text depending on the result of a comparison expression evaluated at preprocessing-time. Its typical use is in the middle of an expression; it avoids splitting it to put a conditional in the middle.

This intrinsic define (macro) differs from the IIF conditional statement in that __FB_IIF__ is evaluated at compile-time only and returns source code text. IIF is evaluated at compile-time only if the compare-expr is a constant. Otherwise IIF expressions are evaluated at run-time.

__FB_ILLUMOS__.name: __FB_ILLUMOS__
__FB_ILLUMOS__.title: __FB_ILLUMOS__
__FB_ILLUMOS__.description:
Define without a value created at compile time when the illumos target is being used. The sunos target spelling also selects the illumos target.

When compiling for illumos, the compiler also defines __FB_SOLARIS__ for Solaris-family compatibility.

__FB_JOIN__.name: __FB_JOIN__
__FB_JOIN__.title: __FB_JOIN__
__FB_JOIN__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro) performed by the compiler.
__FB_JOIN__.description: Joins two token arguments together as one, similar to token pasting operator () but more powerfull (will resolve arguments before joining).

__FB_JS__.name: __FB_JS__
__FB_JS__.title: __FB_JS__
__FB_JS__.description:
Define without a value created at compile time when the JavaScript target is being used. This is normally selected by fbc-js or by the -target js-asmjs command line option. It can be used to compile parts of a program only for the browser/Emscripten target.

The JavaScript target also defines __FB_LINUX__ for compatibility with Emscripten's POSIX-like runtime environment.

__FB_LANG__.name: __FB_LANG__
__FB_LANG__.title: __FB_LANG__
__FB_LANG__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro value) set by the compiler
__FB_LANG__.description:
__FB_LANG__ indicates which language compatibility option was set at the time of compilation of a module. By default __FB_LANG__ will be set to "fb". The language compatibility option can be changed using one (or more) of the following methods: - -lang command line option - -forcelang command line option - #lang directive - $lang metacommand

Returns a lower case string with one of the following values:

__FB_LANG__ is always defined.

__FB_LINUX__.name: __FB_LINUX__
__FB_LINUX__.title: __FB_LINUX__
__FB_LINUX__.summary: Intrinsic define set by the compiler
__FB_LINUX__.description: Define without a value created at compile time when compiling to the Linux target. Default in the Linux hosted version of the compiler, or active when the -target linux command line option is used. It can be used to compile parts of the program only if the target is Linux.

__FB_LOONGARCH64__.name: __FB_LOONGARCH64__
__FB_LOONGARCH64__.title: __FB_LOONGARCH64__
__FB_LOONGARCH64__.summary: Intrinsic define set by the compiler
__FB_LOONGARCH64__.description: Define created at compile time if the compilation target uses the 64-bit LoongArch CPU architecture, otherwise undefined.

__FB_M68K__.name: __FB_M68K__
__FB_M68K__.title: __FB_M68K__
__FB_M68K__.summary: Intrinsic define set for Motorola 68000-family targets.
__FB_M68K__.description: Define without a value created at compile time when the target CPU family is m68k. The current target form is AROS m68k. It also defines __FB_BIGENDIAN__ because the target stores multi-byte values in big-endian order.

__FB_MAIN__.name: __FB_MAIN__
__FB_MAIN__.title: __FB_MAIN__
__FB_MAIN__.summary: Intrinsic define set by the compiler
__FB_MAIN__.description:
__FB_MAIN__ is defined in the main module and not defined in other modules.

The main module is determined by the compiler as either the first source file listed on the command line or explicitly named using the -m option on the command line.

__FB_MIN_VERSION__.name: __FB_MIN_VERSION__
__FB_MIN_VERSION__.title: __FB_MIN_VERSION__
__FB_MIN_VERSION__.summary: Macro function to test minimum compiler version
__FB_MIN_VERSION__.returns: Returns zero (0) if the compiler version is less than the specified version, or non-zero (-1) if the compiler version is greater than or equal to specified version
__FB_MIN_VERSION__.description: __FB_MIN_VERSION__ tests for a minimum version of the compiler.

__FB_MIPS32__.name: __FB_MIPS32__
__FB_MIPS32__.title: __FB_MIPS32__
__FB_MIPS32__.summary: Intrinsic define set for 32-bit MIPS targets.
__FB_MIPS32__.description: Define without a value created at compile time for MIPS32 and MIPS32 little-endian targets. __FB_MIPS__ is defined at the same time. Test __FB_BIGENDIAN__ if byte order changes a data format or hardware interface.

__FB_MIPS64__.name: __FB_MIPS64__
__FB_MIPS64__.title: __FB_MIPS64__
__FB_MIPS64__.summary: Intrinsic define set for 64-bit MIPS targets.
__FB_MIPS64__.description: Define without a value created at compile time for MIPS64 and MIPS64 little-endian targets. __FB_MIPS__ and __FB_64BIT__ are defined at the same time. Test __FB_BIGENDIAN__ if byte order changes a data format or hardware interface.

__FB_MIPS__.name: __FB_MIPS__
__FB_MIPS__.title: __FB_MIPS__
__FB_MIPS__.summary: Intrinsic define shared by 32-bit and 64-bit MIPS targets.
__FB_MIPS__.description: Define without a value created at compile time for every MIPS CPU-family target. The compiler also defines exactly one of __FB_MIPS32__ or __FB_MIPS64__. Big-endian MIPS targets additionally define __FB_BIGENDIAN__.

__FB_MT__.name: __FB_MT__
__FB_MT__.title: __FB_MT__
__FB_MT__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro value) set by the compiler
__FB_MT__.description:
__FB_MT__ indicates if the the multithreaded option -mt was specified on the command line at the time of compilation, or whether one of the ThreadtCreate or ThreadCall keywords is used more above in the source code.

Returns non-zero (-1) if the option was specified. Returns zero (0) otherwise.

__FB_NETBSD__.name: __FB_NETBSD__
__FB_NETBSD__.title: __FB_NETBSD__
__FB_NETBSD__.summary: Intrinsic define set by the compiler
__FB_NETBSD__.description: Define without a value created at compile time in the NetBSD version of the compiler, or when the -target netbsd command line option is used. It can be used to compile parts of the program only if the target is NetBSD.

__FB_NOBUILTINS__.name: __FB_NOBUILTINS__
__FB_NOBUILTINS__.title: __FB_NOBUILTINS__
__FB_NOBUILTINS__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro value) set by the compiler
__FB_NOBUILTINS__.description: Returns non-zero (-1) when -z nobuiltins disables nonessential builtin declarations and definitions, or zero (0) otherwise.

__FB_NOCMDLINE__.name: __FB_NOCMDLINE__
__FB_NOCMDLINE__.title: __FB_NOCMDLINE__
__FB_NOCMDLINE__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro value) set by the compiler
__FB_NOCMDLINE__.description: Returns non-zero (-1) when -z nocmdline disables source #cmdline directives, or zero (0) otherwise. When enabled, the compiler ignores those directives and uses only options passed to fbc.

__FB_NO_FASTCALL__.name: __FB_NO_FASTCALL__
__FB_NO_FASTCALL__.title: __FB_NO_FASTCALL__
__FB_NO_FASTCALL__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro value) set by the compiler
__FB_NO_FASTCALL__.description: Returns non-zero (-1) when -z no-fastcall instructs the compiler to ignore __fastcall directives, or zero (0) otherwise.

__FB_NO_THISCALL__.name: __FB_NO_THISCALL__
__FB_NO_THISCALL__.title: __FB_NO_THISCALL__
__FB_NO_THISCALL__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro value) set by the compiler
__FB_NO_THISCALL__.description: Returns non-zero (-1) when -z no-thiscall instructs the compiler to ignore __thiscall directives, or zero (0) otherwise.

__FB_NUTTX__.name: __FB_NUTTX__
__FB_NUTTX__.title: __FB_NUTTX__
__FB_NUTTX__.summary: Intrinsic define set for the NuttX target.
__FB_NUTTX__.description: Define without a value created at compile time when the experimental NuttX target is selected. The current compiler target is nuttx-riscv32. Board, driver, and Kconfig availability must still be checked separately because the define identifies the operating-system target, not a particular board configuration.

__FB_OPENBSD__.name: __FB_OPENBSD__
__FB_OPENBSD__.title: __FB_OPENBSD__
__FB_OPENBSD__.summary: Intrinsic define set by the compiler
__FB_OPENBSD__.description: Define without a value created at compile time in the OpenBSD version of the compiler, or when the -target openbsd command line option is used. It can be used to compile parts of the program only if the target is OpenBSD.

__FB_OPTABSTRACT__.name: __FB_OPTABSTRACT__
__FB_OPTABSTRACT__.title: __FB_OPTABSTRACT__
__FB_OPTABSTRACT__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro value) set by the compiler
__FB_OPTABSTRACT__.description: Returns non-zero (-1) when -z optabstract prevents unused pure abstract types from being emitted, or zero (0) otherwise.

__FB_OPTIMIZE__.name: __FB_OPTIMIZE__
__FB_OPTIMIZE__.title: __FB_OPTIMIZE__
__FB_OPTIMIZE__.summary: Intrinsic define set by the compiler
__FB_OPTIMIZE__.description: Always defined and will have a value from 0 to 3 (0 by default) to indicate the optimization level passed to the backend compiler via -O.

__FB_OPTION_BYVAL__.name: __FB_OPTION_BYVAL__
__FB_OPTION_BYVAL__.title: __FB_OPTION_BYVAL__
__FB_OPTION_BYVAL__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro value) set by the compiler
__FB_OPTION_BYVAL__.description:
Indicates if parameters to a Function or Sub are passed by reference as with Byref, or by value as with Byval by default when the by value / by reference specifier is not explicitly stated.

__FB_OPTION_BYVAL__ is set to non-zero (-1) if by default parameters are passed value, and zero (0) if by default parameters are passed by reference.

The default for passing parameters by reference or by value is determined by the -lang command line option used during compilation or usage of Option Byval in the source file.

__FB_OPTION_DYNAMIC__.name: __FB_OPTION_DYNAMIC__
__FB_OPTION_DYNAMIC__.title: __FB_OPTION_DYNAMIC__
__FB_OPTION_DYNAMIC__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro value) set by the compiler
__FB_OPTION_DYNAMIC__.description: __FB_OPTION_DYNAMIC__ is defined as true (negative one (-1)) if a recent Option Dynamic statement or '$Dynamic meta-command was issued. Otherwise, it is defined as zero (0).

__FB_OPTION_ESCAPE__.name: __FB_OPTION_ESCAPE__
__FB_OPTION_ESCAPE__.title: __FB_OPTION_ESCAPE__
__FB_OPTION_ESCAPE__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro value) set by the compiler
__FB_OPTION_ESCAPE__.description:
Indicates if by default, string literals are processed for escape characters when not explicitly prefixed with the $ operator for non-escaped strings, or the ! operator for escaped strings.

The default method for processing string literals is set by usage of the -lang command line option during compilation or usage of Option Escape in the source file.

__FB_OPTION_ESCAPE__ returns zero (0) if the option has not been set. Returns non-zero (-1) if the option has been set.

__FB_OPTION_EXPLICIT__.name: __FB_OPTION_EXPLICIT__
__FB_OPTION_EXPLICIT__.title: __FB_OPTION_EXPLICIT__
__FB_OPTION_EXPLICIT__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro value) set by the compiler
__FB_OPTION_EXPLICIT__.description:
__FB_OPTION_EXPLICIT__ indicates if Option Explicit has been used previously in the source.

Returns zero (0) if the option has not been set. Returns non-zero (-1) if the option has been set.

__FB_OPTION_GOSUB__.name: __FB_OPTION_GOSUB__
__FB_OPTION_GOSUB__.title: __FB_OPTION_GOSUB__
__FB_OPTION_GOSUB__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro value) set by the compiler
__FB_OPTION_GOSUB__.description:
Indicates how Gosub and Return will be handled at compile time. If the option is set (-1) then Gosub is allowed and Return is recognized as return-from-gosub only. If the option is not set (0) then Gosub is not allowed and Return is recognized as return-from-procedure only.

This macro value can be changed at compile time. Option Gosub will set the option (enable gosub support) and Option Nogosub will clear the option (disable gosub support).

__FB_OPTION_GOSUB__ returns zero (0) if the option has not been set. Returns non-zero (-1) if the option has been set.

__FB_OPTION_PRIVATE__.name: __FB_OPTION_PRIVATE__
__FB_OPTION_PRIVATE__.title: __FB_OPTION_PRIVATE__
__FB_OPTION_PRIVATE__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro value) set by the compiler
__FB_OPTION_PRIVATE__.description:
Indicates if by default Function's and Sub's have module scope or global scope when not explicitly specified with Private or Public.

The default scope specifier for functions and subs is set by usage of the -lang command line option during compilation or usage of Option Private in the source file.

Default scope of procedures can be changed during compilation with #pragma private.

__FB_OPTION_PRIVATE__ returns zero (0) if the option has not been set. Returns non-zero (-1) if the option has been set.

__FB_OPTION_PROFILE__.name: __FB_OPTION_PROFILE__
__FB_OPTION_PROFILE__.title: __FB_OPTION_PROFILE__
__FB_OPTION_PROFILE__.summary: Intrinsic define set by the compiler
__FB_OPTION_PROFILE__.description:
Intrinsic define set to an integer to indicate that the profiling code is generated: __FB_OPTION_PROFILE__ is set to non-zero when profiling code is generated __FB_OPTION_PROFILE__ is set to zero when profiling code is not generated

#pragma profile allows to control the generation of profiling code. This allows optionally including or excluding sections of source code to be profiled: when #pragma profile = true, then profiling code is generated when #pragma profile = false, then profiling code is not generated

__FB_OUT_DLL__.name: __FB_OUT_DLL__
__FB_OUT_DLL__.title: __FB_OUT_DLL__
__FB_OUT_DLL__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro value) set by the compiler
__FB_OUT_DLL__.description:
__FB_OUT_DLL__ indicates that the specified output file type on the compiler command line at the time of compilation is a shared library.

Returns non-zero (-1) if the output is a shared library. Returns zero (0) otherwise.

Only one of __FB_OUT_DLL__, __FB_OUT_EXE__, __FB_OUT_LIB__, or __FB_OUT_OBJ__ will evaluate to non-zero (-1). All others will evaluate to zero (0).

__FB_OUT_EXE__.name: __FB_OUT_EXE__
__FB_OUT_EXE__.title: __FB_OUT_EXE__
__FB_OUT_EXE__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro value) set by the compiler
__FB_OUT_EXE__.description:
__FB_OUT_EXE__ indicates that the specified output file type on the compiler command line at the time of compilation is an executable.

Returns non-zero (-1) if the output is an executable. Returns zero (0) otherwise.

Only one of __FB_OUT_DLL__, __FB_OUT_EXE__, __FB_OUT_LIB__, or __FB_OUT_OBJ__ will evaluate to non-zero (-1). All others will evaluate to zero (0).

__FB_OUT_LIB__.name: __FB_OUT_LIB__
__FB_OUT_LIB__.title: __FB_OUT_LIB__
__FB_OUT_LIB__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro value) set by the compiler
__FB_OUT_LIB__.description:
__FB_OUT_LIB__ indicates that the specified output file type on the compiler command line at the time of compilation is a static library.

Returns non-zero (-1) if the output is a static library. Returns zero (0) otherwise.

Only one of __FB_OUT_DLL__, __FB_OUT_EXE__, __FB_OUT_LIB__, or __FB_OUT_OBJ__ will evaluate to non-zero (-1). All others will evaluate to zero (0).

__FB_OUT_OBJ__.name: __FB_OUT_OBJ__
__FB_OUT_OBJ__.title: __FB_OUT_OBJ__
__FB_OUT_OBJ__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro value) set by the compiler
__FB_OUT_OBJ__.description:
__FB_OUT_OBJ__ indicates that the specified output file type on the compiler command line at the time of compilation is an object module.

Returns non-zero (-1) if the output is an object module. Returns zero (0) otherwise.

Only one of __FB_OUT_DLL__, __FB_OUT_EXE__, __FB_OUT_LIB__, or __FB_OUT_OBJ__, will evaluate to non-zero (-1). All others will evaluate to zero (0).

__FB_PCOS__.name: __FB_PCOS__
__FB_PCOS__.title: __FB_PCOS__
__FB_PCOS__.summary: Intrinsic define set by the compiler
__FB_PCOS__.description: Define created at compile time if the OS has filesystem behavior styled like common PC OSes, e.g. DOS, Windows, OS/2, Symbian OS, possibly others. Drive letters, backslashes, that stuff, otherwise undefined.

__FB_PIC__.name: __FB_PIC__
__FB_PIC__.title: __FB_PIC__
__FB_PIC__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro value) set by the compiler
__FB_PIC__.description: Returns non-zero (-1) when position-independent code is active, or zero (0) otherwise. The compiler may enable this mode implicitly when required by the target or output type, as well as when -pic is used.

__FB_PPC__.name: __FB_PPC__
__FB_PPC__.title: __FB_PPC__
__FB_PPC__.summary: Intrinsic define set by the compiler
__FB_PPC__.description: Define created at compile time if the compilation target uses the PowerPC CPU architecture, otherwise undefined.

__FB_PROFILE__.name: __FB_PROFILE__
__FB_PROFILE__.title: __FB_PROFILE__
__FB_PROFILE__.summary: Intrinsic define set by the compiler
__FB_PROFILE__.description: Intrinsic define set to an integer to indicate the profiling method. The different value are defined in the ./inc/fbc-int/profile.bi include file (inside Namespace: FB and Enum: PROFGEN_ID): - PROFGEN_ID_NONE: profiling is not enabled - PROFGEN_ID_GMON: code is being generated for gmon/gprof - PROFGEN_ID_CALLS: code is being generated for fb's function call profiler - PROFGEN_ID_CYCLES: code is being generated for fb's cycle count call profiler

__FB_QUERY_SYMBOL__.name: __FB_QUERY_SYMBOL__
__FB_QUERY_SYMBOL__.title: __FB_QUERY_SYMBOL__
__FB_QUERY_SYMBOL__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro) performed by the compiler, and its associated sub-macros.
__FB_QUERY_SYMBOL__.usage:
The ./inc/fbc-int/symbol.bi header exposes internals of the fbc compiler through the built-in macro __FB_QUERY_SYMBOL__.
In addition, many convenient sub-macros with 'is' as name prefix (also defined in the file ./inc/fbc-int/symbol.bi) help the user to indirectly call the generic built-in macro __FB_QUERY_SYMBOL__:
#include once "fbc-int/symbol.bi"
using FBC
' then:
Dim b As Boolean
...
b = isXXXXX( sym )
__FB_QUERY_SYMBOL__.description:
__FB_QUERY_SYMBOL__ is a generic built-in macro for querying fbc symbol internals.

In the file ./inc/fbc-int/symbol.bi, many convenient and specialized sub-macros with 'is' as name prefix ('isXXXXX') are also defined (where 'XXXXX' stands for the kind of query). They help the user to indirectly call the generic built-in macro __FB_QUERY_SYMBOL__ without knowing the encoding of its first parameter and its return value, but passing the only sym parameter to those sub-macros which only return -1 (for True) or 0 (for False).

For three of the query types, convenient and specialized sub-macros are available: - 'class of symbols' (like variable, constant, procedure, namespace, ...), - 'class of data' (like integer, float, string, UDT, ...), - 'type of data' (like boolean, byte, ubyte, short, ...). in order to test whether a symbol matches an element of the considered family.

__FB_QUOTE__.name: __FB_QUOTE__
__FB_QUOTE__.title: __FB_QUOTE__
__FB_QUOTE__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro) performed by the compiler.
__FB_QUOTE__.description: Converts the argument to a string, similar to stringize operator (#) but can be used anywhere (will expand the argument before conversion). More precisely, __FB_QUOTE__ returns an over-quoted text (prefixed with the Operator $ (Non-Escaped String Literal)) compared to the one passed through the argument (the argument may already be a string, and so the return will be an over-quoted string in this case).

__FB_RETURN_IN_FLTS__.name: __FB_RETURN_IN_FLTS__
__FB_RETURN_IN_FLTS__.title: __FB_RETURN_IN_FLTS__
__FB_RETURN_IN_FLTS__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro value) set by the compiler
__FB_RETURN_IN_FLTS__.description: Returns non-zero (-1) when -z retinflts enables returning supported structures in floating-point registers, or zero (0) otherwise.

__FB_RISCOS__.name: __FB_RISCOS__
__FB_RISCOS__.title: __FB_RISCOS__
__FB_RISCOS__.summary: Intrinsic define set for the RISC OS target.
__FB_RISCOS__.description: Define without a value created at compile time when the RISC OS target is selected. It can guard code that uses RISC OS system calls, filesystem rules, package layout, or direct-screen behavior.

__FB_RISCV32__.name: __FB_RISCV32__
__FB_RISCV32__.title: __FB_RISCV32__
__FB_RISCV32__.summary: Intrinsic define set for 32-bit RISC-V targets.
__FB_RISCV32__.description: Define without a value created at compile time when the target CPU family is 32-bit RISC-V. The current use is the experimental nuttx-riscv32 target. This define identifies the CPU family; use __FB_NUTTX__ when code depends on NuttX.

__FB_RISCV64__.name: __FB_RISCV64__
__FB_RISCV64__.title: __FB_RISCV64__
__FB_RISCV64__.summary: Intrinsic define set by the compiler
__FB_RISCV64__.description: Define created at compile time if the compilation target uses the 64-bit RISC-V CPU architecture, otherwise undefined.

__FB_S390X__.name: __FB_S390X__
__FB_S390X__.title: __FB_S390X__
__FB_S390X__.summary: Intrinsic define set by the compiler
__FB_S390X__.description: Define created at compile time if the compilation target uses the s390x CPU architecture, otherwise undefined.

__FB_SIGNATURE__.name: __FB_SIGNATURE__
__FB_SIGNATURE__.title: __FB_SIGNATURE__
__FB_SIGNATURE__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro string) set by the compiler
__FB_SIGNATURE__.description: Substituted by a signature of the compiler where used.

__FB_SOLARIS__.name: __FB_SOLARIS__
__FB_SOLARIS__.title: __FB_SOLARIS__
__FB_SOLARIS__.description:
Define without a value created at compile time when the Solaris target is being used.

The compiler also defines __FB_SOLARIS__ for the illumos target as a Solaris-family compatibility symbol. Use __FB_ILLUMOS__ when code must detect illumos specifically.

__FB_SSE__.name: __FB_SSE__
__FB_SSE__.title: __FB_SSE__
__FB_SSE__.summary: Intrinsic define set by the compiler
__FB_SSE__.description: Define without a value created at compile time if SSE floating point arithmetics is enabled.

__FB_UNIQUEID_POP__.name: __FB_UNIQUEID_POP__
__FB_UNIQUEID_POP__.title: __FB_UNIQUEID_POP__
__FB_UNIQUEID_POP__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro) performed by the compiler.
__FB_UNIQUEID_POP__.description:
Pops an identifier off of stack identified by stack-id (the size of the stack is decreased by 1). (__FB_UNIQUEID__ allows to get the identifier at the top of the stack, and __FB_UNIQUEID_PUSH__ allows to push a new unique identifier on to the stack)

Note: - The "stack-id" name itself is a separate namespace from all other symbols. - The stack can only contain "unique identifiers". - "unique identifier" is a name of an fb symbol that is unique to the module, so does not conflict or shadow other symbol names ("unique identifier" will have the form "LT_xxxx" as a name so it might not be completely unique). - fb uses the form "LT_xxxx" internally for labels, symbols, temp variables, etc (so should avoid naming fbc symbols of this form for any fbc program since version 0.0).

When such a stack is no longer in use, it is recommended that it be empty (at the end there must have been applied as many __FB_UNIQUEID_POP__ as __FB_UNIQUEID_PUSH__ for this stack). At any time of its use, the number of __FB_UNIQUEID_POP__ applied from the beginning must always be less than or equal to the number of __FB_UNIQUEID_PUSH__ applied.

__FB_UNIQUEID_PUSH__.name: __FB_UNIQUEID_PUSH__
__FB_UNIQUEID_PUSH__.title: __FB_UNIQUEID_PUSH__
__FB_UNIQUEID_PUSH__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro) performed by the compiler.
__FB_UNIQUEID_PUSH__.description:
Pushes a new unique identifier on to a stack identified by stack-id (the size of the stack is increased by 1). (__FB_UNIQUEID__ allows to get the identifier at the top of the stack, and __FB_UNIQUEID_POP__ allows to pop an identifier off of the stack)

Note: - The "stack-id" name itself is a separate namespace from all other symbols. - The stack can only contain "unique identifiers". - "unique identifier" is a name of an fb symbol that is unique to the module, so does not conflict or shadow other symbol names ("unique identifier" will have the form "LT_xxxx" as a name so it might not be completely unique). - fb uses the form "LT_xxxx" internally for labels, symbols, temp variables, etc (so should avoid naming fbc symbols of this form for any fbc program since version 0.0).

When such a stack is no longer in use, it is recommended that it be empty (at the end there must have been applied as many __FB_UNIQUEID_POP__ as __FB_UNIQUEID_PUSH__ for this stack). At any time of its use, the number of __FB_UNIQUEID_POP__ applied from the beginning must always be less than or equal to the number of __FB_UNIQUEID_PUSH__ applied.

__FB_UNIQUEID__.name: __FB_UNIQUEID__
__FB_UNIQUEID__.title: __FB_UNIQUEID__
__FB_UNIQUEID__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro) performed by the compiler.
__FB_UNIQUEID__.description:
Gets the identifier at the top of stack identified by stack-id (the size of the stack is not modified). (__FB_UNIQUEID_PUSH__ allows to push a new unique identifier on to the stack, and __FB_UNIQUEID_POP__ allows to pop an identifier off of the stack)

Note: - The 'stack-id' name itself is a separate namespace from all other symbols. - The stack can only contain 'unique identifiers'. - 'unique identifier' is a name of an fb symbol that is unique to the module, so does not conflict or shadow other symbol names ('unique identifier' will have the form 'LT_xxxx' as a name so it might not be completely unique). - fb uses the form 'LT_xxxx' internally for labels, symbols, temp variables, etc (so should avoid naming fbc symbols of this form for any fbc program since version 0.0).

__FB_UNIQUEID__ simply expands to unquoted text. So the name, for example 'Lt_0004', can be used wherever an fb symbol is required (a variable, procedure name, type name, etc.). __FB_UNIQUEID__ returns an unquoted empty string when the stack is empty or has never been filled.

__FB_UNIX__.name: __FB_UNIX__
__FB_UNIX__.title: __FB_UNIX__
__FB_UNIX__.summary: Intrinsic define set by the compiler
__FB_UNIX__.description: Define created at compile time if the OS is reasonably enough like UNIX that you can call it UNIX, otherwise undefined.

__FB_UNQUOTE__.name: __FB_UNQUOTE__
__FB_UNQUOTE__.title: __FB_UNQUOTE__
__FB_UNQUOTE__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro) performed by the compiler.
__FB_UNQUOTE__.description: Takes a literal string and converts it back to tokens. More precisely, __FB_UNQUOTE__ returns a sub-quoted text compared to the one passed through the argument (the argument may already be an over-quoted string, and so the return will be a simple string in this case).

__FB_VALIST_AS_PTR__.name: __FB_VALIST_AS_PTR__
__FB_VALIST_AS_PTR__.title: __FB_VALIST_AS_PTR__
__FB_VALIST_AS_PTR__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro value) set by the compiler
__FB_VALIST_AS_PTR__.description: Returns non-zero (-1) when -z valist-as-ptr represents variadic argument lists with pointer expressions where supported, or zero (0) otherwise.

__FB_VECTORIZE__.name: __FB_VECTORIZE__
__FB_VECTORIZE__.title: __FB_VECTORIZE__
__FB_VECTORIZE__.summary: Intrinsic define set by the compiler
__FB_VECTORIZE__.description: Defined as the vectorisation level number set by the -vec command-line option.

__FB_VERBOSE__.name: __FB_VERBOSE__
__FB_VERBOSE__.title: __FB_VERBOSE__
__FB_VERBOSE__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro value) set by the compiler
__FB_VERBOSE__.description:
__FB_VERBOSE__ indicates whether verbose mode is active at the current point in compilation.

Returns non-zero (-1) if the -v compiler option has been enabled, including by a source #cmdline directive. Returns zero (0) otherwise.

__FB_VERSION__.name: __FB_VERSION__
__FB_VERSION__.title: __FB_VERSION__
__FB_VERSION__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro string) set by the compiler
__FB_VERSION__.description: Substituted by the version number of the compiler where used.

__FB_VER_MAJOR__.name: __FB_VER_MAJOR__
__FB_VER_MAJOR__.title: __FB_VER_MAJOR__
__FB_VER_MAJOR__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro value) set by the compiler
__FB_VER_MAJOR__.description: __FB_VER_MAJOR__ will return the major version of FreeBASIC currently being used. For example, the major version is 0 for FreeBASIC 0.90, and will remain 0 until FreeBASIC version 1.0 is released.

__FB_VER_MINOR__.name: __FB_VER_MINOR__
__FB_VER_MINOR__.title: __FB_VER_MINOR__
__FB_VER_MINOR__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro value) set by the compiler
__FB_VER_MINOR__.description: __FB_VER_MINOR__ will return the minor version of FreeBASIC currently being used. For FreeBASIC version 0.90.1, for example, the minor version number is 90.

__FB_VER_PATCH__.name: __FB_VER_PATCH__
__FB_VER_PATCH__.title: __FB_VER_PATCH__
__FB_VER_PATCH__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro value) set by the compiler
__FB_VER_PATCH__.description: __FB_VER_PATCH__ will return the patch/subversion/revision number the version of FreeBASIC currently being used. For FreeBASIC 0.18, for example, there were subversions 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6, resulting in versions 0.18.1 through 0.18.6.

__FB_WII__.name: __FB_WII__
__FB_WII__.title: __FB_WII__
__FB_WII__.description: Define without a value created at compile time when the Wii target is being used. This is normally selected by fbc-wii or by the -target wii command line option. It can be used to compile parts of a program only for the Wii target.

__FB_WIN32__.name: __FB_WIN32__
__FB_WIN32__.title: __FB_WIN32__
__FB_WIN32__.summary: Intrinsic define set by the compiler
__FB_WIN32__.description: Define without a value created at compile time if compiling to the Win (32-bit or 64-bit) target. Default in Win hosted version, or active if the -target win32 or -target win64 command line option is used. It can be used to compile parts of the program only if the target is Win.

__FB_WINCE__.name: __FB_WINCE__
__FB_WINCE__.title: __FB_WINCE__
__FB_WINCE__.summary: Intrinsic define set for the Windows CE target.
__FB_WINCE__.description: Define without a value created at compile time for the wince-arm and wince-mips targets. Windows CE also defines __FB_WIN32__ so shared Windows data-model declarations remain available. Use __FB_WINCE__ when code depends specifically on the CE API or its reduced CRT.

__FB_X86__.name: __FB_X86__
__FB_X86__.title: __FB_X86__
__FB_X86__.summary: Intrinsic define set by the compiler
__FB_X86__.description: Define created at compile time if the compilation target uses the X86 or X86_64 CPU architecture, otherwise undefined.

__FB_XBOX__.name: __FB_XBOX__
__FB_XBOX__.title: __FB_XBOX__
__FB_XBOX__.description: Define without a value created at compile time when the original Xbox target is being used. It can be used to compile parts of a program only for the Xbox target.

__FILE_NQ__.name: __FILE_NQ__
__FILE_NQ__.title: __FILE_NQ__
__FILE_NQ__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro string) set by the compiler
__FILE_NQ__.description: Substituted with the non-quoted source file name where used.

__FILE__.name: __FILE__
__FILE__.title: __FILE__
__FILE__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro string) set by the compiler
__FILE__.description:
Substituted with the quoted source file name where used.

An example of normal use is to report wrong values in debugging.

__FUNCTION_NQ__.name: __FUNCTION_NQ__
__FUNCTION_NQ__.title: __FUNCTION_NQ__
__FUNCTION_NQ__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro string) set by the compiler
__FUNCTION_NQ__.description:
Substituted with the non-quoted name of the current function block where used.

If __FUNCTION_NQ__ is used at the module level, the function name given will be __FB_MAINPROC__ for the main module, or __FB_MODLEVELPROC__ for a different module. This is not the actual function name though, so it's not as useful there.

__FUNCTION__.name: __FUNCTION__
__FUNCTION__.title: __FUNCTION__
__FUNCTION__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro string) set by the compiler
__FUNCTION__.description:
Substituted with the quoted name of the current function block where used.

Its normal use is to report wrong values in debugging.

If __FUNCTION__ is used at the module level, the function name given will be "__FB_MAINPROC__" for the main module, or "__FB_MODLEVELPROC__" for a different module.

__LINE__.name: __LINE__
__LINE__.title: __LINE__
__LINE__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro value) set by the compiler
__LINE__.description:
Substituted with the current line number of the source file where used.

Its normal use is to report wrong values in debugging.

__PATH__.name: __PATH__
__PATH__.title: __PATH__
__PATH__.summary: Intrinsic define (macro string) set by the compiler
__PATH__.description: Set to the quoted absolute path of the source file at the time of compilation.

__THISCALL.name: __THISCALL
__THISCALL.title: __THISCALL
__THISCALL.summary: Specifies the Thiscall calling convention in a procedure declaration
__THISCALL.usage:
declare Sub name __Thiscall Overload] Alias "alias"] ( parameters )
declare Function name __Thiscall Overload] Alias "alias"] ( parameters ) [ Byref ] as return_type
Sub name [__Thiscall] Overload] Alias "alias"] ( parameters )
Function name [__Thiscall] Overload] Alias "alias"] ( parameters ) [ Byref ] as return_type
__THISCALL.description:
Thiscall is a calling convention for x86 targets where the first integral argument is passed in the ECX register instead of on the stack. All other arguments are passed right to left and callee cleans up the stack (like Stdcall).

On win32 x86, mingw+gcc will use Thiscall as the default calling convention for non-static member procedures in classes passing the hidden This parameter by ECX register instead of pushing to the stack.

Default calling convention on win32 x86 inside an extern "c++" block for non-static member procedures is Thiscall.

Thiscall can be explicitly specified for normal procedures and static member procedures to override the default calling convention. Other calling conventions (Cdecl/Stdcall/etc) can be explicitly specified to override the default Thiscall calling convention on non-static member procedures.

Thiscall can be specified at both the declaration and the definition. If a procedure definition has a declaration (with calling convention explicit or by default) and the definition does not explicitly specify a calling convention, then the calling convention is implied by the declaration.

__TIME__.title: __TIME__

__TIME__.description: Substitutes the compiler time in a literal string (24 clock, "hh:mm:ss" format) where used.
